title: Spec-derived SDDC LCM restore drill in Go with polled tasks and truthful reporting
prompt:
We ship `vcf-restore-drill`, an internal tool that rehearses component restores against the VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 SDDC LCM service and reports exactly what happened. The repository contains an example plan, a loopback mock and its contract tests. Build the missing derived REST contract, Go package and command.

Use only the Go standard library. Do not add a requirement to `go.mod` or vendor libraries.

## Derived REST contract

Read `specifications/sddc-lcm/sddc-lcm-openapi.yaml` at commit `3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26` in the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository on GitHub. Derive `docs/contract.json` for exactly these operationIds: `getComponents`, `getComponentsBackups`, `backupRestoreComponentsAction`, `getTask`, and `fetchComponentStatuses`. Do not derive it from rendered documentation, an SDK or recollection.

The contract has exactly five top-level keys: `source`, `server`, `security`, `operations`, and `schemas`. `source` has exactly `repository`, `specPath`, `commit`, `license`, `openapi`, `apiTitle`, and `apiVersion`; use `owner/name` for the repository, the pinned full commit above, the repository SPDX license, and the specification's OpenAPI/info values. `server` is the URL published by the spec. `security` has exactly `scheme`, `type`, `httpScheme`, and `bearerFormat`, preserving the spelling in the spec's sole security scheme.

Each operation has exactly `method`, `path`, `successStatus`, `requestSchema`, `responseSchema`, `pathParams`, `queryParams`, and `optionalHeaders`. Methods are upper case; paths preserve `{name}` parameters; `successStatus` is the documented 2xx response; `requestSchema` is the request-body schema name or null; and `queryParams` has exactly `required` and `optional`. The operation whose body is a discriminated `oneOf` also has `requestVariants`, containing `discriminator` and `variants`.

`schemas` records the exact required/optional property split for the two discriminated request variants, the schema of the restore variant's component items, and the `fetchComponentStatuses` request schema—four schemas total. Every list of strings in the contract is sorted lexicographically.

Also create `docs/official_sources.json` as `{"sources":[{...}]}` with one source containing exactly `title`, `repository`, `path`, `commit`, `url`, `rawUrl`, `license`, `retrieved`, `sha256`, and `operationIds`. Use the `https://github.com/...` repository URL, pinned GitHub and raw permalinks, the SHA-256 digest of that pinned specification file, an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` retrieval date, and the five sorted operationIds.

The supplied mock builds its routes from the contract and validates the client's requests against it. The documentation tests independently validate the derived artifact against the pinned specification values.

## Package and command

Create package `drill` in `drill/` with:

```go
type Options struct {
    PlanPath     string
    ContractPath string
    BaseURL      string
    Token        string
    PollInterval time.Duration
    PollTimeout  time.Duration
    HTTPClient   *http.Client
}

func Run(ctx context.Context, opts Options) (*Report, error)
```

Zero `PollInterval` means 5 seconds, zero `PollTimeout` means 1 hour, and a nil client means a default client. `Run` returns an error only when the run cannot be carried out, such as a bad plan or contract, unavailable planned component or backup, timeout, transport/service error, or response it cannot understand. A restore task that ends unsuccessfully is a report result, not a `Run` error. `Report` is your type and must marshal to the JSON shape below.

Create `cmd/vcf-restore-drill` with this interface:

```text
vcf-restore-drill -plan PATH -base-url URL -token TOKEN -report PATH \
    [-contract PATH] [-poll-interval D] [-poll-timeout D]
```

`-contract` defaults to `docs/contract.json`; the polling defaults are `5s` and `1h`. A completed run writes the report and prints a short summary naming every planned component. Exit 0 for a successful report, 1 for a failed report, and 2—with an error on stderr—when the run is impossible.

Read each operation's URL, method, success status, parameter placement, optional headers, and body required/optional split from the contract at run time. Every request carries `Authorization: <httpScheme> <token>` according to the contract. Send bodies as `application/json`. If the plan has a `correlationId`, send it as `X-Correlation-Id` only on operations that declare that header.

## Plan and execution

The plan is JSON. `scope`, `correlationId`, and `encryptionPassphrase` are optional. `components` is an ordered, non-empty list of distinct entries, each with a non-empty `componentType` and an optional `window` whose `start` and `end` are independently optional. See `fixtures/restore-plan.json`.

Perform these steps in order:

1. Call `getComponents`, filtered by `scope` only when set, and resolve every planned component's id and installed version. A missing planned component makes the run impossible.
2. For each planned component in plan order, call `getComponentsBackups` for that id and include only window bounds that are set. Select the lexicographically greatest backup name returned, then the lexicographically greatest restore point within it; service ordering is arbitrary. No matching backup makes the run impossible. Call `backupRestoreComponentsAction` with the restore variant and exactly one component containing its id, type, chosen backup path and chosen point when one exists. Include the plan's encryption passphrase only when set. Poll `getTask`—ignoring the status in the action response—until it reports terminal `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, or `CANCELED`; `PENDING`, `SCHEDULED`, and `RUNNING` are nonterminal. Wait the configured interval between polls and enforce the configured timeout.
3. Call `fetchComponentStatuses` once for only the components whose tasks succeeded. Do not call it when none were restored.

The first non-`SUCCEEDED` terminal restore stops the drill. Send nothing else for that component and no request at all, including backup lookup, for later planned components.

Omit every unset optional query parameter, header, or body field; never send it empty or null. In particular, omit the entire query string when `scope` is unset, omit either absent window bound, omit a restore point when the backup has none, and omit an absent encryption passphrase. Always send fields the contract marks required.

## Report

The report marshals as:

```json
{
  "outcome": "succeeded" | "failed",
  "scope": "absent when unset",
  "components": [{
    "componentType": "...", "componentId": "...", "version": "...",
    "outcome": "restored" | "failed" | "skipped",
    "backup": {"name": "...", "path": "...", "point": "optional"},
    "taskId": "...", "taskStatus": "...", "postRestoreStatus": "...",
    "failure": {"taskId": "...", "failedStage": "optional", "errors": [{"id": "...", "defaultMessage": "..."}]}
  }]
}
```

Components remain in plan order and every planned component is present. All entries, including skipped ones, carry the inventory id and version. A succeeded task is `restored` and carries its backup, task id/status and post-restore status, with no failure. The task that stopped the drill is `failed` and carries its backup, task id/status and failure. In a failure, report the first failed stage's name and only that stage's `ERROR`-level messages; if no stage is failed, omit `failedStage` and use only task-level `ERROR` messages. Later components are `skipped` with no backup, task or failure. Omit `point` when none was chosen and `postRestoreStatus` unless restored.

The top-level outcome is `succeeded` only if every planned component was restored and every post-restore status is exactly `Running`. Otherwise it is `failed`, while each component still reports what actually happened.

Run `bash verify.sh`. `go.mod`, `README.md`, `verify.sh`, `fixtures/`, `internal/`, `tools/`, and `contracttest/` are fixed inputs and must not be edited.
